subject: Physics
prompt: Impedance of series RLC circuit
explain: Net reactance is (X_L−X_C); impedance combines this with R by Pythagoras.

subject: Physics
prompt: Resonance condition in series RLC
explain: At resonance inductive and capacitive reactances cancel; Z = R (minimum).

subject: Physics
prompt: RMS value of sinusoidal current I₀sinωt
explain: For a sine wave, RMS = peak/√2 ≈ 0.707 × peak value.

subject: Physics
prompt: Average power in AC circuit
explain: cosφ is the power factor; only the resistive component dissipates power.

subject: Physics
prompt: Power factor of a pure inductor
explain: Pure inductor has φ = 90°; cos90° = 0, so no real power is consumed.

subject: Physics
prompt: Phase of current relative to voltage in pure capacitor
explain: In a capacitor, charge (and hence current) leads voltage by π/2.

subject: Physics
prompt: Inductive reactance X_L depends on frequency as
explain: X_L = 2πfL increases linearly with frequency.

subject: Physics
prompt: Capacitive reactance X_C depends on frequency as
explain: X_C = 1/(2πfC) decreases as frequency increases.

subject: Physics
prompt: Quality factor Q of series RLC at resonance
explain: Q measures sharpness of resonance; higher Q → narrower bandwidth.

subject: Physics
prompt: Bandwidth of series RLC resonance circuit
explain: Bandwidth Δω = R/L; Q = ω₀/Δω relates sharpness to bandwidth.

subject: Physics
prompt: Wattless current flows in which element?
explain: Reactive (wattless) current flows in L or C; it contributes no average power.

subject: Physics
prompt: Transformer turns ratio and voltage relation
explain: Secondary voltage scales with turns ratio; step-up if N_s > N_p.

subject: Physics
prompt: In ideal transformer, power relation is
explain: Ideal transformer conserves power; input power equals output power.

subject: Physics
prompt: At resonance, voltage across L (or C) vs applied voltage
explain: V_L = I·X_L = (V/R)·ω₀L = QV; voltage magnification equals Q factor.

subject: Physics
prompt: Phase angle φ in series RLC is given by
explain: φ = tan⁻¹[(X_L−X_C)/R]; positive φ means inductive (current lags).

subject: Physics
prompt: Average value of sin-wave current over full cycle
explain: Positive and negative half-cycles cancel; average over full period = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: Average (mean) value of |I| over a half-cycle
explain: Average of rectified sine over half period = 2/π × peak ≈ 0.637 I₀.

subject: Physics
prompt: Form factor of a sinusoidal AC wave
explain: Form factor = RMS/average = (I₀/√2)/(2I₀/π) = π/(2√2) ≈ 1.11.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a pure resistor, phase difference between V and I is
explain: Resistor obeys Ohm's law instantaneously; V and I are always in phase.

subject: Physics
prompt: Energy stored in inductor in AC circuit (average)
explain: Average magnetic energy = ½L·I_rms² = ½L·(I₀/√2)² = ¼LI₀².

subject: Physics
prompt: Current in series RLC at resonance equals
explain: At resonance Z = R (minimum), so current is maximum = V₀/R.

subject: Physics
prompt: SI unit of impedance Z
explain: Impedance Z = V/I has the same unit as resistance: Ohm (Ω).

subject: Physics
prompt: Power factor cosφ for series RLC equals
explain: cosφ = R/Z; ranges from 0 (pure reactive) to 1 (pure resistive).

subject: Physics
prompt: Which loss is NOT present in an ideal transformer?
explain: Ideal transformer assumes zero winding resistance and no core losses.

subject: Physics
prompt: Domestic AC supply in India: frequency and rms voltage
explain: Indian standard AC supply is 50 Hz frequency with 220 V rms.

subject: Physics
prompt: Peak voltage V₀ relates to rms voltage V_rms by:
explain: For sinusoidal wave, peak value = √2 × rms value.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a pure inductor, current lags voltage by:
explain: In a pure inductor, current lags applied voltage by exactly 90° (π/2).

subject: Physics
prompt: Impedance of a pure capacitor of capacitance C at frequency ω:
explain: Pure capacitor has only capacitive reactance X_C = 1/ωC as its impedance.

subject: Physics
prompt: Impedance of a pure inductor L at angular frequency ω:
explain: Pure inductor has only inductive reactance X_L = ωL as its impedance.

subject: Physics
prompt: In series RLC, current leads voltage when:
explain: When capacitive reactance exceeds inductive reactance, circuit is capacitive; current leads.

subject: Physics
prompt: Average power dissipated in a pure capacitor is:
explain: Pure capacitor has power factor = 0, so average power dissipated is zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: Resonant frequency of series LC circuit:
explain: At resonance X_L = X_C gives ω₀ = 1/√(LC).

subject: Physics
prompt: In a transformer, if N₂ > N₁, it is a:
explain: Secondary turns > primary turns means secondary voltage > primary voltage: step-up.

subject: Physics
prompt: Secondary current I₂ vs primary current I₁ in ideal transformer:
explain: Power conservation: V₁I₁ = V₂I₂, so I₁N₁ = I₂N₂ (currents inversely as turns).

subject: Physics
prompt: Impedance of series RL circuit (no C):
explain: For RL series: Z = √(R² + X_L²) = √(R² + ω²L²).

subject: Physics
prompt: Impedance of series RC circuit (no L):
explain: For RC series: Z = √(R² + X_C²) = √(R² + 1/ω²C²).

subject: Physics
prompt: The unit of reactance (X_L or X_C) is:
explain: Reactance has SI unit ohm (Ω), same as resistance and impedance.

subject: Physics
prompt: AC generator works on the principle of:
explain: AC generator converts mechanical energy to electrical using Faraday's law of EM induction.

subject: Physics
prompt: EMF induced in a rotating coil (N turns, area A, field B, ω):
explain: ε = −dΦ/dt = NBAω sinωt; peak emf ε₀ = NBAω.

subject: Physics
prompt: Power factor of a series RLC circuit at resonance:
explain: At resonance X_L = X_C, φ = 0, so power factor cosφ = 1 (purely resistive).

subject: Physics
prompt: Choke coil (inductor) is preferred over resistor to control AC because:
explain: Choke (pure inductor) has power factor ≈ 0, so average power dissipation ≈ zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: If V = V₀ sinωt across a capacitor, current i through it is:
explain: i = C·dV/dt = CωV₀ cosωt; current leads voltage by 90° in capacitor.

subject: Physics
prompt: Energy stored in a capacitor in AC circuit (average):
explain: Average energy ½CV² averaged over cycle gives ½C·V_rms² (since <sin²> = ½).

subject: Physics
prompt: At resonance in series RLC, which quantity is maximum?
explain: At resonance Z is minimum (= R), so current amplitude I₀ = V₀/R is maximum.

subject: Physics
prompt: Sharpness of resonance in series RLC increases when:
explain: Q = ω₀L/R; lower resistance gives higher Q factor and sharper resonance peak.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which loss in a real transformer is reduced by using laminated core?
explain: Laminated core breaks eddy current paths, drastically reducing eddy current (iron) losses.

subject: Physics
prompt: Dimension of LC (product of inductance and capacitance):
explain: ω₀ = 1/√(LC), so √(LC) = 1/ω has dimension T; hence LC has dimension T².

subject: Physics
prompt: Phase difference between voltage across R and voltage across L in series RL circuit:
explain: V_R is in phase with current; V_L leads current by 90°; so V_R and V_L differ by 90°.

subject: Physics
prompt: In series RLC, V_L and V_C are always:
explain: V_L leads current by 90° and V_C lags by 90°, so they are mutually 180° apart.

subject: Physics
prompt: Frequency of AC at which a capacitor acts as a short circuit:
explain: X_C = 1/ωC → 0 as ω → ∞; capacitor blocks DC (f = 0) and passes high-frequency AC.
